_hinweis: Vocabulary step on /teachers/lesson and /lesson: for each A1 word field in kursinhalte.json (bloecke[].wortschatz, keys must match exactly) a task for the learners and its words. A word that is a lemma of the A1 list (src/content/lexicon/a1.json) gets its el/la, plural and example sentence from there; a noun the list does not have may be written with its article ("la carta", "el NIE"); phrases without an entry (¡Hola!, letters) are shown as written here. Word fields without an entry only show the general task.

es419.note: Latin America says ustedes for vosotros, celular for móvil, carro or auto for coche, computadora for ordenador, and tomar for coger.

Greetings.aufgabe: Walk around the room. Say hello to three people, ask how they are and say goodbye: once with tú, once with usted.

Countries and nationalities.aufgabe: Ask your partner: «¿De dónde eres?» – «Soy de …». Show the country on a map or on your phone.

Languages.aufgabe: Ask each other: «¿Qué idiomas hablas?» Everyone says two languages. Write all the languages of the class on the board.

The alphabet.aufgabe: Spell your first name and your surnames. Your partner writes them down and reads them back.

Numbers.aufgabe: Count round the class to 20, then in tens to 100. In pairs, dictate three phone numbers to each other. In Spain people often read them in groups: 612 34 56 78.

Address.aufgabe: Ask each other: «¿Dónde vives?» Write down your partner's address: street, number, floor, postcode and town. Spanish addresses read like this: Calle Mayor 12, 3.º B, 50001 Zaragoza.

Email.aufgabe: Dictate an email address to your partner. Your partner writes it down and reads it back.

Forms: nombre, apellidos, domicilio.aufgabe: In pairs, fill in a form for each other: ask, listen, write. In Spain most people have two surnames, so ask for both.

Family.aufgabe: Draw your family tree and explain it to your partner: «Esta es mi madre …»

Married, single ….aufgabe: Ask politely: «¿Está usted casado?» or «¿Estás casada?» Answer for a person you invent.

Describing people.aufgabe: Describe a person in the class. The others guess who it is.

Rooms.aufgabe: Draw your flat or house. Show your partner around: «Esta es la cocina …»

Furniture.aufgabe: Say what is in your living room. Your partner draws it.

Colours.aufgabe: Find something in the room for every colour and say: «La mochila es azul.» Watch the ending: el coche rojo, la casa roja.

grande / pequeño / luminoso.aufgabe: Describe your room with three adjectives. Your partner says if their room is the same.

Food.aufgabe: Write your shopping list for the weekend. Read it to your partner.

Drinks.aufgabe: Ask three people: «¿Qué bebes por la mañana?» Write down the answers.
woerter: Un café con leche, por favor.

Containers (una botella de, un paquete d.aufgabe: Play shop: one person sells, one person buys. Use «una botella de», «un paquete de», «un kilo de».

Prices in euros.aufgabe: Write prices on cards. Your partner asks: «¿Cuánto cuesta?» and you read the price: 3,50 € = tres euros con cincuenta.

Daily routine.aufgabe: Tell your partner about your morning: «Me levanto a las siete. Luego …»

Times of the day.aufgabe: Say what you do at each time of the day. Your partner says one thing for each, too. In Spain, la tarde runs until it gets dark, and lunch is often at two.

Days of the week.aufgabe: Ask each other: «¿Qué haces el lunes?» Make a plan for the week together. Days have no capital letter in Spanish.

Hobbies.aufgabe: Ask three people: «¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?» Find one hobby you share.

Sport.aufgabe: Mime a sport. The others guess it: «¿Juegas al fútbol?»

Music.aufgabe: Ask your partner about music: What do they like? Do they play an instrument?

Weekend.aufgabe: Plan a weekend together: el sábado por la mañana, el sábado por la tarde, el domingo.

Places in town.aufgabe: Draw a small map of your town. Your partner asks: «¿Hay un banco por aquí?»

Directions.aufgabe: Use the map. Explain the way from the station to the bank. Your partner follows it with a finger.

Transport.aufgabe: Ask three people: «¿Cómo vas al trabajo?» Count the answers.

Tickets.aufgabe: Role play at the ticket office: buy a ticket to Valencia.
woerter: Un billete a Valencia, por favor.

The body.aufgabe: One person says a body part, everyone touches it: «¡La cabeza!» Then a learner takes over.

Illness.aufgabe: Mime an illness. The others guess: «¿Te duele la cabeza?»

At the health centre.aufgabe: Role play at the centro de salud: the receptionist asks for your health card, the doctor asks what is wrong.

Asking for an appointment.aufgabe: Role play: phone the centro de salud and ask for an appointment. Find a day and a time that works.

Everyday actions.aufgabe: Mime something. The others guess with estar + gerund: «¿Estás cocinando?» «Sí, estoy cocinando.»

Plans for the weekend.aufgabe: Ask your partner: «¿Qué vas a hacer el fin de semana?» Tell the class one thing.
woerter: Voy a visitar a mi hermana.

hoy, ahora, mañana.aufgabe: Make a timeline on the board: ahora, hoy, esta tarde, mañana, la semana que viene. Everyone adds one sentence.

Jobs.aufgabe: Mime a job. The others guess: «¿Eres profesora?» Spanish has no un or una here: Soy enfermero.

Workplaces.aufgabe: Say where people work: «Un profesor trabaja en un colegio.» Your partner names another job.

Hours and shifts.aufgabe: Ask each other: «¿A qué hora empiezas? ¿A qué hora terminas?» Write down the times. Who has a turno de mañana, who a turno de noche?

Clothes.aufgabe: Describe what a person in the class is wearing. The others guess who it is.

Sizes.aufgabe: Role play in a clothes shop: ask for a different size.

Paying.aufgabe: Role play at the till: the customer pays, the shop assistant asks how. Then ask for the receipt.

Months.aufgabe: Line up by birthday, enero to diciembre. Everyone says their month. Months have no capital letter in Spanish.

Festivals.aufgabe: Tell your partner about a festival in your country: When is it? What do people do? Then name one you know in Spain.

Invitations.aufgabe: Write a short invitation to a party. Your partner says yes or no and gives a reason.

Congratulations.aufgabe: Go round the class: one person names an occasion (a birthday, a new job, a wedding), the next says the right phrase.

Town hall.aufgabe: Role play at the ayuntamiento: ask where the right counter is and what papers you need. The other person works there.

Bank.aufgabe: Role play at the bank: open an account or ask about your card.

Forms.aufgabe: Swap forms with your partner and check them: is every box filled in? Is the date right, day first (03/11/2026)?

Empadronamiento: the words.aufgabe: Read the words together. Then role play at the ayuntamiento: you want to register at your address. This is language practice: what you need in your town is on your ayuntamiento's website.
